subject: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>, Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Hi Emma / Paul —

Great to meet this morning. Per our kickoff, attached is the Redwood test plan we propose to validate performance for the NovaHealth integration and confirm acceptance criteria before production cutover. High level plan below — full doc in Drive (link in metadata).

Objectives:
- Validate steady-state throughput for typical payloads (avg 512 tokens)
- Confirm P95 and P99 latency targets under target concurrency
- Verify KV/prefix caching behavior and cold-start impact
- Produce artifacted logs + CSV results for your audit and our onboarding checklist

Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
- Throughput: sustained 220–250 requests/sec at 512-token average payload
- Latency: P95 <= 120 ms per token and P99 <= 280 ms per token
- Error rate: < 0.5% 5xx across the run

Planned runs (Pacific TZ):
- Warmup: 2026-02-04 02:00–02:30 (30m)
- Primary run: 2026-02-05 02:00–04:00 (2h) — steady-state sweeps at target concurrency
- Regression run (if needed): 2026-02-06 03:00–04:00 (1h)

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-instructions.pdf (run checklist), novahealth-k6-scenarios.yaml (k6 config). Marcus will share the test harness and the endpoint to point at. Dev — can you confirm the model variant and quantization profile we should pin for the runs?

Next steps: please confirm the run windows and who from NovaHealth will own the test execution (engineers / QA). If you want Redwood to run the tests, we can execute them in your Dedicated pool during the scheduled window.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>, Nathan Li <nathan.li@infraqa.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Thanks Soojin — plan looks sensible. A few Qs before we lock windows: 

1) Are the latency targets per-token or end-to-end per-response? For our SLOs we generally measure end-to-end, but the token-based framing may be easier for you to quantify.
2) Can you confirm whether the runs will include function-calling traces? Our usual traffic triggers a small amount of tool calls which inflate latency.
3) For the CSV results, we need per-request trace ids so our infra team can map to internal logs.

We prefer Redwood to run the primary run on 2026-02-05 during your Dedicated window. Emma and Nathan will monitor.

--Paul
Paul Cheng
Director, Platform Engineering — NovaHealth
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>, Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Paul — good questions. Answers below: 

1) Latency framing: The thresholds in Soojin's note are measured as service-side per-token (model decode time) to normalize across payload sizes. For your SLO mapping I’ll include an end-to-end column in the CSV so you can calculate end-to-end P95.
2) Function-calling: we will run the primary sweep without function calls to establish baseline. We can run a separate profile that includes tool calls (+~15–30% latency depending on call complexity).
3) Trace ids: we will include a request_id and redwood_trace_id fields in each CSV row. 

Model pin and runtime details:
- Model: rw-3-small-v1 (quantized int8 profile we discussed)
- Kernel profile: high-throughput (continuous batching enabled)
- Cache policy: prefix caching enabled, cold-start window simulated in warmup run

I attached the k6 scenarios we’ll use (novahealth-k6-scenarios.yaml) and a short run checklist (redwood-benchmark-instructions.pdf). Marcus — endpoint and harness config?

Dev
Dev Patel
SRE / Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>, Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 01:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Hi all — sharing the test harness and run details. Endpoint for primary run (read-only): https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/nh-testbed/endpoint

k6 harness notes:
- Scenario: ramp to 260 RPS over 10m, hold 90m, then cool down 10m
- Payload template: typical NovaHealth prompt (512 token avg) included in yaml
- Headers: include x-nh-request-id (we will echo back)

Attachments uploaded to the shared Drive post-run. I’ll be live in the run window and will push raw CSV to you within 60 minutes of completion.

Attachments: novahealth-k6-scenarios.yaml

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Nathan Li <nathan.li@infraqa.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>, Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2026 04:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Marcus / Dev — thanks for running this. Attached are the raw results from the primary run (novahealth-load-results-20260205.csv). Highlights: 

- Avg throughput observed: 238 RPS over the 2h steady window
- P95 per-token latency: 110 ms (meets threshold)
- P99 per-token latency: 260 ms (meets threshold)
- 5xx error rate: 0.24% (within target)

Notes / anomalies:
- Two transient spikes at 02:38 and 03:11 — trace ids included in CSV; both correlate with cache eviction during a burst of larger payloads (test artifact).
- End-to-end P95 (as NovaHealth measures) corresponds to ~180 ms for the sample set because of client-side post-processing.

We uploaded the CSV and a short run log to the shared Drive. Please confirm receipt and whether this artifact satisfies the acceptance checklist so we can proceed to schedule production route cutover.

Regards,
Nathan Li
QA Lead, InfraQA (third-party test contractor for NovaHealth)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rodriguez <emma.rodriguez@novahealth.ai>, Paul Cheng <p.cheng@novahealth.ai>, Nathan Li <nathan.li@infraqa.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: plan, run windows, and evidence handoff

Emma / Paul / Nathan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed CSV. I reviewed the numbers with Dev and Marcus: the run meets the acceptance thresholds we proposed. The transient spikes are noted as test artifacts and not blockers.

Action items agreed:
- Redwood to produce a one-page acceptance memo and upload to the NovaHealth onboarding folder (I’ll attach it to the HubSpot deal).
- NovaHealth to schedule production route cutover for 2026-02-12 02:00 PT (tentative) — Emma to confirm by Monday.
- Marissa (CS) will own the rollout checklist and coordinate a 1-hour observability handoff session the day of cutover.

If Emma confirms the cutover window, I’ll mark the onboarding milestone as complete and update the deal. Thanks everyone — great teamwork.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
